Hannah / Marissa —

Quick take from GTM/legal coordination:
- Business ask: Acme is asking for an uncapped carve-out for trade secrets. That will be a hard no for finance/ops; it materially changes our risk profile.
- Negotiation posture: offer a narrowly tailored carve-out for "willful misappropriation" with a defined evidentiary standard, injunctive remedies, and a higher but finite cap (e.g., 24 months of fees or $10M, whichever is greater). 
- Rationale: protects us from open-ended exposure while giving Acme meaningful remediation for intentional wrongdoing.

Suggested language (draft):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Limitation of Liability), neither party's liability for damages arising from the other party's willful misappropriation of trade secrets or intentional disclosure of the other's Confidential Information shall exceed the greater of (a) an amount equal to twenty-four (24) months of fees paid or payable under the Order Form, or (b) Ten Million United States Dollars (USD 10,000,000). The foregoing shall not limit the right to seek injunctive or other equitable relief."

Also propose we require Acme to provide a short notice & cure window for non-willful issues and that any claim must be supported by a declaration from senior counsel + all relevant evidence (to reduce frivolous claims).

If legal signs off, I'll present to Acme as our compromise.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Redwood MSA - confidentiality / trade secret carve-out request

Ben/Hannah —

Legal review notes (high level):
1) We can accept a carve-out for "willful misappropriation" but we need: 
   - Clear definition of what constitutes "willful misappropriation" (intent + materiality).
   - An evidentiary standard (certified declaration + supporting documentation).
   - A requirement to pursue injunctive relief prior to/during damages recovery where feasible.
2) Proposed cap: 12–24 months of fees is typical for enterprise deals. $10M floor is acceptable only for large strategic deals; ask finance if ACME estimated ARR/commitment justifies a $10M floor.
3) Add an explicit carve-out for consequential damages only to the extent tied to trade secret misappropriation (i.e., allow direct damages up to the cap; continue to exclude consequential/special damages otherwise).
4) We should add an audit/forensics cooperation clause to limit spurious allegations and to facilitate remediation.

I attached a short playbook with language variants. Recommend we propose 18 months fees / $5M floor as a middle ground unless Ben confirms ACME ARR indicates higher. Also include a mutual indemnity carve-out if appropriate.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@acmehealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood MSA - confidentiality / trade secret carve-out request

Julia —

Thanks for flagging this. We discussed internally and want to propose a targeted compromise that balances Acme's protection need with Redwood's underwriting requirements. Proposed order-form language below; attached is an updated redline of the MSA showing the changes.

Proposed compromise language (for inclusion in Order Form):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Limitation of Liability), in the event of willful misappropriation of trade secrets by Redwood or intentional disclosure of Acme's Confidential Information by Redwood, Redwood's liability for direct damages shall be limited to the greater of (a) eighteen (18) months of fees paid or payable under the Order Form, or (b) Five Million United States Dollars (USD 5,000,000). The parties agree that claims of willful misappropriation shall be supported by a written declaration from Acme's general counsel and corroborating technical forensics. Nothing in this section shall limit either party's right to seek injunctive or other equitable relief."

Additional points:
- We add a mandatory forensics cooperation clause and a short notice/cure step for non-willful disclosures.
- We are not agreeing to an uncapped remedy; this is a narrow carve-out for intentional conduct with a clear evidentiary bar.

If that is acceptable, I can send a clean order form with the language and DocuSign links by EOB. If Acme needs a higher floor (e.g., $10M) or an uncapped option, we will need to elevate to commercial leadership and finance for approval.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
